title: Variant cohesion gate and KV/tokenizer ops regimen for fallback routing
creator: Omar Chen
description:
Goal: Establish an operational gate and ongoing regimen to ensure fallback model variants used by smart routing remain compatible across tokenizer behavior, KV/prefix cache semantics, context length handling, and developer tooling (function calling, structured output). This ticket coordinates automation, dashboards, and runbook updates so routing policies can safely fall back between variants (across regions and customer tiers) without causing tokenization drift, KV cache corruption, or broken SDK behaviors.

Scope:
- Define the test matrix for representative variant families (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, Llama-family forks, T5-derived variants) with permutations for tokenizer version, context window, and KV semantics.
- Implement nightly compatibility sweeps that run small synthetic workloads exercising tokenization boundaries, long-context KV reuse, and tool-calling serialization.
- Add telemetry-driven healthchecks and signal thresholds used by the routing controller to mark a variant as ineligible for fallback.
- Update the runbook and console rollout gating so canary/upgrade jobs fail fast when swap incompatibilities are detected.
- Produce an automated deprecation plan for legacy variants that fail ongoing compatibility checks, including customer notification templates and migration recommendations.

Non-goals: full model correctness/regression detection unrelated to tokenizer/KV/tooling parity (those remain in model QA). This ticket focuses on interoperability for safe runtime fallback and routing resilience.
acceptance_criteria: A test matrix doc exists listing variants, tokenizer versions, KV semantics, and tooling checks
Nightly sweep job completes end-to-end and writes pass/fail signals to the compatibility registry
Routing controller consumes compatibility signals and refuses fallback to variants flagged as incompatible
Console shows per-variant compatibility status in the model catalog UI
Runbook describes steps to triage and roll back routing changes when compatibility regressions are detected
updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff meeting with ML infra, runtime, and console teams. Agreed to build on top of existing compatibility registry (ENG-31207).
2026-02-28: Draft test matrix posted to Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INF/variant-cohesion-matrix). Added initial families and tokenizer pairs for CI jobs.

2026-03-03: Prototype nightly sweep created (pipeline ref: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/PR-842). Sweep runs 1200 small sessions across three variant families exercising tokenizer edge cases and KV prefix reuse.

2026-03-07: Found a tokenizer mismatch between variant X.1 and fallback X.1-legacy when handling Unicode normalization in function calling payloads. Created hotfix branch to normalize inputs at runtime (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/PR-1298).
2026-03-10: Telemetry schema v2 added to model-metrics ingestion to capture compatibility signals (signal keys: variant.compat.tokenizer, variant.compat.kv, variant.compat.tooling).

2026-03-12: Began wiring compatibility signals into routing controller; currently behind feature flag 'routing.compat-check'. Observed 0.3% of fallback attempts blocked in staging due to tokenization drift; investigating owners for two legacy variants.
work_items: Define canonical tokenizer test vectors for each supported tokenizer (owner: ML infra)
Implement KV semantics smoke tests (owner: runtime)
Nightly sweep orchestration and CI integration (owner: infra-ops)
Console UI: per-variant compatibility banner + drilldown (owner: console)
Routing controller: consume registry and add denylist TTL semantics (owner: routing)
Customer migration template and deprecation cadence (owner: solutions)
Add alerting: high failure rate in nightly sweep -> P0 incident paging
risks: False positives in sweeps could unnecessarily reduce available capacity for Hosted fallback routes
Nightly job load could increase infra costs if not throttled by variant family
Telemetry signal delay could cause temporary routing oscillations during model rollouts
mitigations: Use staged thresholds and require 3 consecutive nightly failures before marking variant ineligible
Limit sweep concurrency and sample only representative prefixes per customer cohort
Add canary-only rollout for routing changes that consult compatibility flags before full rollout
